title: Mason General
notes: The cover of this QP says it was deactivated on 01/04/2022. It is the version the CSDCI Mason General assessment guide is built on, and it is loaded only so the mapper can tell a mason from an electrician. Replace it with the current NQR version before any real assessment.

Mapping only: this pack is used to tell a mason from an electrician. Its anchors, observables and the 18 tolerances from the CSDCI Mason General assessment guide are kept for reference, but a deactivated QP is never used to score a candidate.

nos.title: Construct masonry structures using brick / block

elements.title: Carry out preparatory work before starting masonry work
Check material used for brickwork/block work
Lay brick/block for construction of load bearing/non-load bearing wall, columns and footings.
Check the line, level and alignment
Carry out pointing in brick masonry
Perform specialized masonry works such as arches, staircase, manholes, and walkways
Repair and restore brick /block masonry

pcs.text: read and interpret the basic working drawings / sketches before the commencement of brick / block work
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or cannot read the main dimensions, or misreads lengths, openings or wall thickness.
Meets standard: reads wall length, height, thickness and opening positions correctly and explains them before starting work.
Exceeds in places: also picks out service locations and finish details and relates the drawing dimensions to the marks on site.
Excellent: reads the whole drawing quickly and accurately, spots missing or clashing dimensions and asks before building.
observables: Reads length, height and width of the foundation and wall from the drawing
Points out door and window openings and the architectural finish shown
Identifies where plumbing, fire and electrical service points fall in the wall
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 13

pcs.text: ensure tools are in working condition
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or starts work with a loose hammer head, bent straight edge or faulty level without checking.
Meets standard: checks trowel, hammer, straight edge, try square, spirit level, plumb bob and tape before use; keeps out faulty ones.
Exceeds in places: also tests accuracy, such as reversing the spirit level and sighting along the straight edge, and cleans tools first.
Excellent: thorough, quick tool check as a habit; explains how a faulty level or square spoils the work and reports defects.
observables: Checks trowel, hammer and chisel for loose handles, cracks or worn edges
Checks that the straight edge is straight, the spirit level reads true and the plumb bob string is sound
Sets aside a damaged or inaccurate tool and reports it
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 13

pcs.text: set out the layouts as per instructions from superiors
pcs.measurementTask: Tape the overall length of the wall built on the candidate's layout and enter its difference from the drawing length in mm, either way (deviation; the guide sets no fixed target).
observables: Marks the wall layout on the floor with red oxide as per the drawing
Takes every length from one reference line and checks it with a tape
Length of the perpendicular wall is within 4 mm of the drawing
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), pages 13 and 71

tolerance.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 71: Overall length of wall ±4mm

pcs.text: check for adequate roughness/wetting of surface
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or lays mortar on a smooth, dusty or dry base, or leaves dead concrete in place.
Meets standard: checks the base, roughens it where smooth, removes dead concrete and wets it before laying mortar.
Exceeds in places: roughens evenly over the whole bed, clears dust and loose bits, and wets it without leaving puddles.
Excellent: base fully prepared and evenly damp at the right time; explains how a dry or smooth base weakens the bond.
observables: Looks over the base and roughens a smooth surface with a hacking hammer
Chips off dead concrete with a point or flat chisel
Sprays water to wet the surface just before laying mortar, leaving no standing water
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 13

pcs.text: identify and transfer required levels using appropriate tools
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or guesses levels by eye, or marks are wrong because of air in the tube or a moving tube.
Meets standard: transfers the level from the reference mark with a tube level and marks it correctly at each corner.
Exceeds in places: bleeds air from the tube, waits for the water to settle and cross-checks the marks against each other.
Excellent: accurate, quick level transfer to all points; explains the 300 mm reference line and checks marks before use.
observables: Transfers the finished floor level from the reference level with a water tube level
Marks a reference line 300 mm above finished floor level at every corner with marker or paint
Clears air bubbles from the tube and lets the water settle before marking
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 13

pcs.text: visual check for quality of bricks / blocks prior to use
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses under-burnt, over-burnt, cracked or misshapen bricks without sorting.
Meets standard: sorts bricks by eye for burning, size, colour and damage and sets aside unfit ones before laying.
Exceeds in places: also checks the ring by striking bricks together and keeps the best-faced bricks for exposed faces.
Excellent: quick, reliable sorting; explains each defect and how it affects the strength and finish of the wall.
observables: Sets aside over-burnt, under-burnt, broken and cracked bricks
Checks bricks for uniform size and colour with straight, sharp edges
Strikes two bricks together and listens for a clear ringing sound
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 13

pcs.text: ensure fine aggregate is sieved as per grade requirement
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses unsieved sand with stones, lumps or rubbish, or the wrong sieve.
Meets standard: sieves the sand through the 2.36 mm sieve and uses only sieved sand in the mortar.
Exceeds in places: sets the sieve at a steady angle, clears the oversize regularly and keeps sieved sand clean and covered.
Excellent: efficient, correct sieving; explains why grading and silt matter and spots silty sand by rubbing it.
observables: Sieves the sand through a 2.36 mm square-opening sieve before mixing
Removes stones, clay lumps and rubbish from the sand
Keeps sieved sand apart from unsieved sand
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 13

pcs.text: ensure bricks / blocks are soaked prior to use
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or lays dry bricks that suck water from the mortar, or bricks still dripping wet.
Meets standard: soaks bricks in clean water for at least two hours and lays them surface dry but damp.
Exceeds in places: plans soaking ahead so soaked bricks are always ready, and keeps them shaded so they do not dry out.
Excellent: consistent soaking routine; explains how dry bricks weaken the joint and how soaking suits the brick.
observables: Soaks bricks in clean water for at least two hours before laying
Lets surface water drain so bricks are damp, not dripping, when laid
Keeps enough soaked bricks ready for the next part of the work
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 13

pcs.text: appropriate tools and equipments as per the tasks at requirement such as: Different types of Trowels (of the right blade size) Masons Hammer Blocking Chisel Mashing Hammer Jointers
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses the wrong tool, such as a trowel edge to cut bricks, or works without line or level.
Meets standard: selects the right trowel, hammer, chisel, jointer and checking tools for each step and uses them correctly.
Exceeds in places: chooses blade sizes to suit the joint and brick and keeps tools in order so the work flows without stops.
Excellent: complete, well-chosen tool kit used skilfully; explains why each tool suits its task.
observables: Picks a brick trowel for laying and a pointing trowel or jointer for joints
Uses a mason's hammer, or a blocking chisel with a mashing hammer, to cut bricks
Keeps plumb bob, spirit level, try square, straight edge and line and pins at hand
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: break bricks to required shape and size using appropriate tools
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or breaks bricks by guess with a trowel, giving shattered or wrong-size pieces.
Meets standard: marks and cuts bricks with chisel and hammer to the half, three-quarter or closer size needed.
Exceeds in places: scores the brick all round before the final blow, so cuts are clean and little brick is wasted.
Excellent: accurate, clean cuts first time with little waste; names each cut piece and where it goes in the bond.
observables: Marks the cut line on the brick before cutting
Cuts with a brick chisel and hammer, scoring all round before the final blow
Cut pieces such as half bats, three-quarter bats and closers are to size with clean edges
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: estimate the quantity of raw material required
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or cannot estimate, or is so far off that work stops for material or much is wasted.
Meets standard: calculates bricks, cement and sand from the wall size and mortar ratio with a sensible result.
Exceeds in places: shows the working step by step, allows for wastage and the dry volume of mortar, and checks the answer.
Excellent: quick, accurate estimate explained clearly; converts it to bags of cement and loads of sand to order.
observables: Works out the wall volume from length, height and thickness
Calculates the number of bricks and the cement and sand for the mortar ratio
Adds an allowance for wastage and states the totals
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: lay and fix bricks / blocks as per specification within tolerance limit using appropriate mortar/adhesive as per applicability
pcs.measurementTask: Measure bed and vertical joints at several places with a steel scale and enter the reading farthest from 10 mm.
observables: Spreads a 10 mm mortar bed and fills every vertical joint with mortar
Lays to the specified bond, alternating courses so that vertical joints do not line up
Uses brick closers where the drawing and the bond need them
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 14

tolerance.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 71: Regular joint thickness ±3mm; page 31: Mortar Thickness: 10mm

pcs.text: maintain that rise of brick work / block work is in line & level
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or builds without line or level, so courses wave, slope or step as the wall rises.
Meets standard: raises the corners first, lays each course to a tight line and keeps the rise in line and level.
Exceeds in places: keeps course heights even by marking courses on the corners and corrects small errors before the mortar sets.
Excellent: wall rises true course after course with no correction needed; explains how errors build up if unchecked.
observables: Builds the corners first and checks them for plumb, alignment and level
Ties a masons line between the corner bricks and lays each course to it
Checks plumb, alignment and level at every course as the wall rises
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: ensure proper curing of constructed masonry structure
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or no curing, or the wall is left to dry out in the first days.
Meets standard: dates the wall and keeps the masonry wet for at least 7 days without washing out joints.
Exceeds in places: cures at regular intervals through the day, wetting both faces and the top, and shades it in hot weather.
Excellent: reliable curing routine; explains how curing gives the mortar its strength and what happens without it.
observables: Writes the date of construction on the wall
Keeps the brickwork wet continuously for at least 7 days
Starts curing once the mortar has set, without washing out fresh joints
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 14

pcs.text: maintain required level and specified slope for construction
pcs.measurementTask: Check the top course with a spirit level or tube level against the required level and enter the largest deviation in mm (deviation; the guide sets no fixed target).
observables: Builds to the reference level marks transferred before laying
Checks the level of each course with a spirit level
Gives the slope shown on the drawing where one is specified, such as on a sill
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 14

tolerance.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 71: Level to top course ±5mm

pcs.text: check vertical and horizontal alignment using appropriate tools
pcs.measurementTask: Hold a plumb bob or long spirit level on the wall face over its full height and enter the largest deviation from plumb in mm (deviation; the guide sets no fixed target).
observables: Checks plumb at the corners and along the face with a plumb bob or spirit level
Checks horizontal alignment with a masons line along each course
Corrects a brick out of plumb or line while the mortar is still green
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 14

tolerance.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 71: Plumb to overall height ±5mm

pcs.text: maintain line and level of each course of brickwork using wooden / aluminium straight edge sections
pcs.measurementTask: Stretch a line or hold the straight edge along the wall face over up to 3 m and enter the largest offset from straight in mm (deviation; the guide sets no fixed target).
observables: Places a wooden or aluminium straight edge along each course to check line and level
Taps bricks into line while the mortar is green
Wall face shows no bulges, hollows or stepped courses
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 14

tolerance.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 71: Wall alignment (up to 3meter) ±5mm

pcs.text: set out 90 corners using builders square or 3-4-5 method and check right angle
pcs.measurementTask: Check the internal corner with a builder's square or the 3-4-5 diagonal and enter the deviation from square in mm (deviation; the guide sets no fixed target).
observables: Places a builder's square between the two walls to check the right angle
Sets out the 90 degree corner by the 3-4-5 method and checks it
Squareness on the other side of the corner is within 5 mm
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), pages 14 and 71

tolerance.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 71: Internal square ness ±4mm

pcs.text: perform proper pointing and raking of joint to obtain desired surface for exposed brick work
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or joints are raked too shallow or unevenly, or the pointing is patchy and smears the bricks.
Meets standard: rakes joints 15 to 20 mm, cleans and wets them and points them evenly to the required finish.
Exceeds in places: raking depth is uniform throughout, pointing lines are crisp and straight and the brick faces are left clean.
Excellent: neat, uniform pointing fit for exposed face work; explains the purpose of each step.
observables: Rakes out the mortar joints to a depth of 15 to 20 mm
Cleans and wets the raked joints before pointing
Finished joints are even in width and depth and the brick face is cleaned with brush or sponge
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: ensure proper bonding with old and new surface
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or puts new mortar on a dusty, dry old surface with no slurry, so it will not bond.
Meets standard: cleans and wets the old surface, applies bonding agent or slurry, then rich mortar, and cures the work.
Exceeds in places: applies the new mortar while the slurry is still tacky and leaves a clean, tight junction with no gaps.
Excellent: sound, neat joint between old and new work; explains why slurry and wetting are needed for the bond.
observables: Rakes out loose and dry mortar and washes the old surface with water
Applies a bonding agent or cement slurry on the old surface before new mortar
Uses rich cement mortar, cleans spills with a wet sponge and cures for at least 7 days
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: ensure lime/cement mortar for pointing is prepared as per specification
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or mixes by guess with no measured ratio, or the mortar is too wet, lumpy or setting.
Meets standard: measures cement or lime and sand to the specified ratio and mixes a uniform mortar of the right stiffness.
Exceeds in places: uses a gauge box for exact batches, mixes small fresh batches and keeps the mortar shaded.
Excellent: correct pointing mortar batch after batch; explains the ratio, when lime or cement is used, and its working time.
observables: Measures binder and sand by volume for the specified pointing ratio
Mixes dry to an even colour before adding water
Mortar is stiff and workable and is used while fresh
pcs.observablesSource: Derived from the PC text

pcs.text: fill joints with appropriate mortar to obtain specified type of pointing
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or joints are left hollow or part filled, or mortar is smeared over the brick face.
Meets standard: fills each cleaned, wet joint fully and firmly with the right mortar, ready for the specified pointing.
Exceeds in places: fills deep joints in layers so they are solid, keeps the fill depth uniform and keeps faces clean.
Excellent: every joint solidly filled and neat; explains how hollow joints let water in and crack the pointing.
observables: Cleans and wets each raked joint before filling
Presses fresh mortar firmly into the joint with a pointing tool, leaving no voids
Removes surplus mortar from the brick face with brush or sponge
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: carry out various types of pointing works as per specification using appropriate tools and technique
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or cannot form the pointing asked for, or the profile is uneven and smeared.
Meets standard: forms the specified pointing types with suitable tools to a uniform, clean profile.
Exceeds in places: handles several types well, with crisp edges and even depth, and slopes weathered joints to shed water.
Excellent: all six types formed neatly and quickly; explains where each type is used and why.
observables: Produces flush, grooved, recessed, weathered, struck and raked pointing as asked
Uses the right jointer or pointing tool for each profile
Each profile is uniform along the whole joint
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: ensure proper curing of pointing
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or the pointing is left to dry, or curing water washes out the fresh joints.
Meets standard: keeps the pointing damp for 7 days, starting once the mortar has set, without damaging it.
Exceeds in places: cures regularly through each day and shades the work in hot or windy weather.
Excellent: reliable curing routine; explains how drying too fast causes cracked and loose pointing.
observables: Starts curing once the pointing mortar has set
Keeps the pointing damp for 7 days
Sprays gently so fresh pointing is not washed out
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: maintain set out of tread and riser of staircase as per drawing/instruction
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or steps are uneven in rise or tread, or the flight does not fit the drawing.
Meets standard: sets out and builds the steps with risers and treads to the drawing sizes, each level and equal.
Exceeds in places: divides the total height into equal risers before starting, so the last step fits without adjustment.
Excellent: accurate, uniform flight first time; explains why equal risers matter for safety and checks each step.
observables: Marks the stair layout from the drawing and transfers the level from the reference level
Builds each riser to the required height, such as 150 mm, and each tread to its width, such as 300 mm
All risers and treads are equal and each tread is level
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: maintain masonry works as per required bond, alignment and plumb
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or the bond is broken with continuous vertical joints, or the work is visibly out of plumb or line.
Meets standard: keeps the required bond, alignment and plumb throughout, checking every course.
Exceeds in places: places closers and cut bricks neatly so the bond pattern is regular on both faces.
Excellent: flawless bond, line and plumb in special work such as piers and returns; explains each bond choice.
observables: Follows the specified bond, with closers placed as per the drawing
Alternates courses so no vertical joints line up
Checks plumb, alignment and level at every course
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 15

pcs.text: maintain bricks/block for manholes as per required line & level and providing channels and benching
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or walls out of line or plumb, openings misplaced, or channel and benching missing or flat.
Meets standard: builds the chamber to size, line and plumb with correct inlet and outlet, channel and sloping benching.
Exceeds in places: channel runs smoothly at the right fall from inlet to outlet and the benching is finished smooth.
Excellent: neat, accurate chamber that drains fully; explains why channel fall and benching slope prevent blockage.
observables: Marks the manhole layout on the PCC as per the drawing
Leaves inlet and outlet openings at the right places and checks plumb, alignment and level
Forms the channel and slopes the benching towards it
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 16

pcs.text: lay and fix paver block to designed pattern & finish the joints as specified
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or the pattern is wrong, pavers rock or sit at uneven levels, or edge gaps are left open.
Meets standard: lays pavers on a levelled sand bed in the designed pattern, to level and slope, with joints finished as specified.
Exceeds in places: joints are straight and even, cut pieces fit neatly at the edges and the surface is checked with a straight edge.
Excellent: flat, firm, true pattern with neat cuts and filled joints; explains the sand bed and the need for edge restraint.
observables: Fixes level button marks about every 2 m and screeds a 20 mm sand bed to them
Lays pavers from one end in the designed pattern with tight, even joints
Taps pavers to level and fills edge gaps with cut pieces
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 16

pcs.text: install anchors and ties for masonry arches
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or anchors and ties are missing, loose, or away from the drawing positions.
Meets standard: marks and fixes the specified anchors and ties firmly at the drawing positions.
Exceeds in places: checks the spacing and level of each tie before fixing and beds each one fully in mortar.
Excellent: all anchors and ties accurately placed and secure; explains how they hold the arch to the backing wall.
observables: Marks the anchor and tie positions from the drawing
Fixes the specified anchors and ties at those positions, firmly bedded in mortar
Ties sit at the right level and spacing and do not obstruct the arch units
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 16

pcs.text: install arch masonry unit by laying and aligning as per specified bond
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or the arch bricks are not radial, the bond is broken or the arch face is out of plumb.
Meets standard: lays the arch units on the layout in the specified bond, radial and in line, closing at the crown.
Exceeds in places: keeps the wedge-shaped joints even, works equally from both sides and fixes the key brick tightly.
Excellent: true, symmetrical arch with a neat bond; explains springing, crown and key brick and when the centering can come off.
observables: Marks out the arch from the drawing before laying
Lays the arch bricks in the specified bond, radially, from both springings towards the crown
Checks plumb and alignment of the arch face at every course
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 16

pcs.text: cut creepers around corners and full joints to obtain a flushed structure
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or pieces are cut by guess, chipped or ill fitting, leaving gaps or projections at corners.
Meets standard: marks and machine-cuts pieces to size so they fit around corners with full joints and a flush face.
Exceeds in places: cuts are clean and square, the machine is used safely with guard and PPE, and waste is small.
Excellent: precise cuts that sit flush first time; explains marking, safe cutting and how full joints keep out water.
observables: Marks the cut on each brick as per the specification
Cuts the pieces with a brick cutting machine, wearing eye and ear protection
Cut pieces fit around the corners with full joints and a flush face
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 16

pcs.text: ensure proper curing of constructed masonry structure
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or no curing, or the new work is loaded, walked on or left to dry out.
Meets standard: dates the work and keeps it wet for at least 7 days, protecting it from early loading.
Exceeds in places: uses ponding or wet sacking where suited, such as on steps and benching, and cures every face.
Excellent: complete, well-planned curing of all special work; explains why arches and steps need care before loading.
observables: Writes the date on the masonry with marker or paint
Keeps arches, steps, manholes and other work wet for at least 7 days
Keeps fresh work from being walked on or loaded while it cures
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 16

pcs.text: remove deteriorated elements from masonry structures using tools such as saws drills and chisels without causing damage to adjacent structure
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or hacks bricks out with heavy blows that crack or loosen the surrounding work.
Meets standard: removes the damaged bricks and mortar with saw, drill or chisel without damaging the adjacent work.
Exceeds in places: cuts the joints first so bricks come out cleanly, and supports the masonry above while working.
Excellent: careful, controlled removal with no damage around it; explains the sequence and the support needed.
observables: Marks the damaged area and props the work above if needed before cutting out
Cuts the joints around damaged bricks with saw, drill or chisel, working from the centre outwards
Removes the old bricks and mortar without loosening the bricks around them
pcs.observablesSource: Derived from the PC text

pcs.text: reinstall brick/block to match previous or existing work
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or the new bricks clearly differ in size or bond, or are loose or hollow jointed.
Meets standard: relays matching bricks in the existing bond, line and joint size, fully bedded and jointed.
Exceeds in places: matches colour and texture closely and packs the top joint tightly so the repair takes load.
Excellent: repair blends in and is structurally sound; explains how mismatched bricks or joints show and fail.
observables: Uses bricks that match the old ones in size, colour and texture
Follows the existing bond and joint thickness
Packs the top joint solidly so the new bricks carry load
pcs.observablesSource: Derived from the PC text

pcs.text: perform proper pointing and raking of joint to obtain desired surface for exposed brick work
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or raking is shallow or damages the brick edges, or the new pointing differs badly from the old.
Meets standard: rakes out to 15 to 20 mm, cleans and wets the joints and repoints to match the existing work.
Exceeds in places: raking is uniform, brick edges stay sharp and the new pointing blends in colour and profile.
Excellent: repointing hard to tell from the original and fully sound; explains the repair sequence.
observables: Rakes old joints out to 15 to 20 mm without chipping brick edges
Cleans and wets the joints before repointing
New pointing matches the existing profile and the surface is cleaned with brush or sponge
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 17

pcs.text: ensure proper bonding with old and new surface
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or new work is placed on dry, dusty old masonry with no slurry, leaving a weak joint.
Meets standard: prepares, wets and slurries the old surface, bonds the new work to it and cures the junction.
Exceeds in places: keys the new courses into the old work by toothing, so the junction will not crack.
Excellent: repair fully bonded and clean; explains why toothing, slurry and curing stop a crack at the junction.
observables: Rakes out loose mortar and washes the old surface
Applies bonding agent or cement slurry to the old work before new mortar
Cleans spilled mortar with a wet sponge and cures for at least 7 days
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 17

nos.title: Execute plaster on internal & external surfaces of Masonry & RCC structures

elements.title: Carry out preparatory work before starting the plastering work
Check material used for plastering
Plaster internal & external masonry & RCC structures
Check for line , level & alignment

pcs.text: read sketches for plastering work
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or misreads thickness, finish or openings, so the plaster is planned wrongly.
Meets standard: reads plaster area, thickness, finish type, openings and service positions correctly from the sketch.
Exceeds in places: relates the sketch to the actual wall and notes where services must go in before plastering.
Excellent: reads the sketch fully and quickly, spots missing details and asks before work starts.
observables: Reads the plaster area, thickness and finish type from the sketch
Notes door and window openings and service points such as pipes and switch boxes
Explains the plastering sequence the sketch calls for
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 17

pcs.text: select correct materials, tools, tackles and equipments, handle and store it properly at workplace
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses damaged or wrong tools, or leaves cement bags on a damp floor or uncovered.
Meets standard: selects suitable plastering materials and tools, checks them and handles and stores them properly.
Exceeds in places: stacks cement off the floor and away from walls, keeps sand clean and cleans tools after use.
Excellent: tidy, well-organised workplace with everything ready; explains the storage rules and why they matter.
observables: Selects plastering trowel, wooden and metal floats, straight edge, plumb bob and spirit level
Checks that the tools are clean and undamaged before use
Stacks cement bags on a raised platform, away from walls and covered

Exceeds in places: checks the base level at several points and corrects soft or low spots before starting.
Excellent: firm, true sub-base prepared efficiently; explains how a poor base causes settlement and cracks.
observables: Clears the base of loose soil, roots and debris
Levels the base to the required level
Wets and compacts the base before the first course
pcs.observablesSource: Derived from the PC text

pcs.text: ensure proper compaction of base prior to commencement of work
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or starts laying on loose, uncompacted ground.
Meets standard: compacts the base properly before laying, so it is firm and even.
Exceeds in places: compacts in layers at the right moisture and checks firmness across the whole area.
Excellent: thorough, efficient compaction; explains how moisture and layer depth affect it.
observables: Compacts the base with a rammer or plate compactor before laying stones
Wets the base to suit compaction
Base does not yield underfoot when compaction is complete
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), pages 21 and 29

pcs.text: select the particular type of surface finish as per the site requirements
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or cannot name or choose a finish, or dresses stones to the wrong finish.
Meets standard: selects the finish the drawing or site needs and dresses the face stones to it.
Exceeds in places: keeps the finish uniform over the whole face and matches it to existing work.
Excellent: chooses and produces finishes confidently; explains where each finish suits and why.
observables: Reads the required face finish from the drawing or the site condition
Names finishes such as hammer dressed, fine chiselled, tooled and pitched face
Dresses the face stones to the chosen finish
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 21

pcs.text: prepare the sides, edges, bed of stone to ensure proper bonding of stones
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or lays stones with rounded beds or thin edges, so they rock or wedge apart.
Meets standard: dresses sides, edges and beds so each stone sits firm and bonds with its neighbours.
Exceeds in places: trial fits stones before bedding and dresses only as much as needed, with little waste.
Excellent: stones fit snugly with little mortar needed; explains how good beds and sides give a strong bond.
observables: Checks the sides, edges and bed of each stone are fit for laying
Knocks off weak corners and thin edges and dresses a firm bed
Trial fits each stone before bedding it in mortar
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 21

pcs.text: mix mortar for rubble masonry in specified ratio including dry & wet mix
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or mixes by guess, adds water before dry mixing, or uses mortar that has set.
Meets standard: dry mixes to the specified ratio, then wets only the mortar that can be used within 30 minutes.
Exceeds in places: uses a gauge box for batching and keeps the consistency the same from batch to batch.
Excellent: correct, fresh mortar throughout; explains why mortar that has begun to set is not remixed with water.
observables: Batches cement and sand to the specified ratio, such as 1:6
Mixes dry to an even colour before adding water
Wets only as much mortar as can be used within 30 minutes
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 21

pcs.text: identify and transfer required levels using appropriate tools prior to rubble
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or starts without levels, so the courses and top level drift.
Meets standard: transfers and marks the required levels with a tube level before starting the masonry.
Exceeds in places: marks levels at all corners and checks them against each other.
Excellent: accurate level marks set quickly; explains how they control course heights and the top level.
observables: Transfers the level from the reference level with a tube level
Marks a reference line 300 mm above finished level at all corners
Fixes course and top levels before laying starts
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 21

pcs.text: check for workability and proportion of cement mortar
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses mortar that is too stiff, too wet or of unknown proportion.
Meets standard: checks the cement, the proportion used and the workability of the mortar before laying.
Exceeds in places: adjusts water to keep workability steady and rejects mortar that has begun to stiffen.
Excellent: consistent, workable mortar throughout; explains the effect of too much or too little water.
observables: Checks cement bags for grade, batch date and week of manufacture
Confirms the mortar proportion matches the specification
Mortar is plastic and holds on the trowel without being runny
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 21

pcs.text: check the quality of stones used in random rubble masonry
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses cracked, weathered or undersized stones without checking.
Meets standard: checks stones for soundness, size, colour and finish and sorts face and filling stones.
Exceeds in places: tests doubtful stones by striking them and sets aside long stones for bond stones.
Excellent: sound stone selection throughout; explains signs of poor stone and the needs of face, hearting and bond.
observables: Checks the stones are as specified and free of cracks and weathering
Checks the stones for size, colour, finish and damage
Keeps dressed stones for the face and undressed stones for filling
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), pages 21 and 65

pcs.text: ensure proper soaking of stones prior to laying
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or lays dry, dusty stones that draw water from the mortar.
Meets standard: soaks and cleans stones before laying so they are damp when bedded.
Exceeds in places: keeps a stock of soaked stones ready and re-wets those left in the sun.
Excellent: consistent soaking routine; explains how dry or dusty stones weaken the mortar bond.
observables: Soaks or wets the stones before laying
Washes dust and mud off the stones
Stones are damp, not dripping, when laid
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 21

pcs.text: work with both undressed and hammer dressed stones as per the requirement of the construction site
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or cannot tell when to dress a stone, or dresses every stone needlessly.
Meets standard: uses hammer dressed stones where required and undressed stones where they suit, as the site needs.
Exceeds in places: dresses efficiently, picking stones that need little work, and keeps the face appearance even.
Excellent: skilled with both kinds of stone; explains when dressing is needed and how much.
observables: Uses hammer dressed stones on the face where required
Uses undressed stones for hearting and filling
Dresses stones with a hammer only where the site needs it
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 21

pcs.text: lay stones to build wall of un-course random rubble or course random rubble as per instruction
pcs.measurementTask: Tape the overall length of the finished wall along its face and enter the length in mm.
observables: Uses dressed stones on the face and undressed stones for filling
Staggers vertical joints and uses enough bond stones through the wall
Length of the perpendicular wall is within 4 mm of the drawing
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), pages 21, 45 and 74

tolerance.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 74: Overall length of wall ±4mm; page 42: 1500 mm (task drawing)

pcs.text: knock off all projecting corners of the laid stones with joints filled and flushed as per the requirements of the site for the un-course random rubble masonry
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or projecting corners are left, joints are hollow, or the face is rough and uneven.
Meets standard: knocks off projections and fills joints fully and flush, giving an even face as the site requires.
Exceeds in places: joints are well packed with chips, regular in width and neatly flushed, with no mortar smeared on stones.
Excellent: even, tight face with solid, regular joints; explains why projections and hollow joints weaken the wall.
observables: Knocks off projecting corners of the laid stones so the face is even
Packs joints fully with mortar and stone chips
Makes face joints flush where no plaster follows, not more than 20 mm thick
Joints are of regular thickness, within 5 mm either way (the page 65 sheet says 3 mm)
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), pages 45, 65 and 74

pcs.text: use large stones at the corners and at jambs to increase the strength as per the un-course random rubble masonry requirements
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses small or rounded stones at corners and jambs, leaving weak, loose corners.
Meets standard: places large, well-shaped stones at corners and jambs, bonded into both faces.
Exceeds in places: corner stones alternate in direction course by course, tying the two walls together.
Excellent: strong, true corners and jambs; explains how large corner stones tie the walls and resist cracking.
observables: Places large, well-shaped stones at the corners and jambs
Corner stones bond alternately into both walls
Places the largest stones in the lowest course
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 45

pcs.text: ensure proper curing of rubble masonry structure
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or no curing, or the wall is left to dry out in the first days.
Meets standard: cures the rubble masonry by a suitable method for at least 7 days.
Exceeds in places: cures regularly through each day and covers the top in hot or windy weather.
Excellent: reliable curing routine; explains how curing builds mortar strength in thick stone walls.
observables: Uses a suitable curing method, such as spraying or wet sacking
Cures the masonry for at least 7 days
Keeps both faces and the top damp
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 22

pcs.text: perform raking of joints as specified prior to drying of bonding mortar
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or raking waits until the mortar hardens, or is shallow and uneven.
Meets standard: rakes joints to the specified depth while the mortar is green, evenly along the joints.
Exceeds in places: keeps a uniform depth with square backs and no damage to stone edges.
Excellent: clean, uniform raking at the right time; explains how it keys the pointing to the wall.
observables: Rakes joints to a depth of 15 to 20 mm
Rakes while the mortar is still green
Raked joints are even, with no loose mortar left
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 22

pcs.text: ensure that joints are cleaned and surface is wet prior to pointing
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or points into dusty, dry joints.
Meets standard: cleans out the raked joints and wets them and the surface before pointing.
Exceeds in places: re-wets joints that dry out and checks each joint is clean to its full depth.
Excellent: joints always clean and damp; explains how dust and dryness make pointing fall out.
observables: Brushes dust and loose mortar out of the raked joints
Wets the joints and stone surface before pointing
Joints are damp, not running with water, when pointing starts
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 22

pcs.text: ensure lime/cement mortar for pointing is prepared as per specification
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or mixes pointing mortar by guess, or the mortar is coarse, wet or stale.
Meets standard: prepares pointing mortar to the specified ratio with fine sand, mixed evenly and used fresh.
Exceeds in places: batches accurately and keeps colour and consistency the same across batches.
Excellent: consistent, correct pointing mortar; explains when lime or cement mortar suits stone work.
observables: Batches binder and sand to the specified pointing ratio
Uses fine sieved sand and mixes dry to an even colour
Mixes small batches so the mortar is used fresh
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 22

pcs.text: fill joints with appropriate mortar to obtain specified type of pointing
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or joints are left hollow, or overfilled and smeared over the stones.
Meets standard: fills all joints fully with fresh mortar, ready to form the specified pointing.
Exceeds in places: presses mortar in layers into deep joints and keeps the stone faces clean.
Excellent: joints solidly filled and neat throughout; explains how the fill affects durability.
observables: Presses fresh mortar firmly into the cleaned, wet joints
Fills joints fully to the depth needed for the specified pointing
Keeps stone faces free of smeared mortar, cleaning with brush or sponge
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 22

pcs.text: carry out various types of pointing works as per specification using appropriate tools and technique
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or cannot form the pointing asked for, or the profile is uneven and smeared.
Meets standard: forms the specified pointing types, such as V and struck, with suitable tools to a clean profile.
Exceeds in places: profiles are uniform along the irregular stone joints and the edges are crisp.
Excellent: neat pointing of several types on rubble work; explains where each type is used.
observables: Forms V pointing and struck pointing as specified
Uses the right pointing tool for each profile
Cleans the stone surface with brush or sponge after pointing
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), pages 22 and 42

pcs.text: ensure proper curing of pointing
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or the pointing is left to dry, or washed out by heavy watering.
Meets standard: keeps the pointing damp for at least 7 days by a damp method, starting once it has set.
Exceeds in places: cures regularly through each day and shades the work in hot sun.
Excellent: reliable curing; explains how early drying cracks the pointing and lets water in.
observables: Keeps the pointing damp for at least 7 days
Uses a damp method, such as wet sacking or gentle spraying
Starts curing once the pointing has set
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 22

pcs.text: lay and fix stones for construction of walls without use of mortar
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or stones rock or slip because they are not fitted, packed or bonded.
Meets standard: builds a stable dry wall with stones fitted and packed firmly and joints broken.
Exceeds in places: keeps the face true and uses through stones at intervals for stability.
Excellent: tight, stable dry walling with a good bond; explains how weight and fit hold it without mortar.
observables: Selects and fits stones so each sits firm without mortar
Packs the gaps with small stones and spalls so no stone rocks
Breaks vertical joints and places through stones across the wall
pcs.observablesSource: Derived from the PC text

pcs.text: knock off all projecting corner
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or projections are left, or trimming loosens or cracks the laid stones.
Meets standard: trims projecting corners with a stone chisel so the face is even.
Exceeds in places: trims with controlled blows so stones stay firm and the edges are clean.
Excellent: even, neat face with every projection removed safely; explains why projections are removed.
observables: Trims projecting corners with a stone chisel
Face of the wall is even after trimming
Trims without loosening the stone in the wall
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 22

pcs.text: mark and transfer required levels at a regular interval in order to maintain proper slope of finished surface in case of horizontal surface
pcs.measurementTask: Check the top course with a spirit level or tube level against the required level and enter the largest deviation in mm (deviation; the guide sets no fixed target).
observables: Transfers the finished level from the reference level with a tube level
Marks a reference line 300 mm above finished level at all corners
Brings the top course to the marked level, giving any specified slope
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 22

tolerance.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 74: Level to top course ±5mm

pcs.text: check horizontal and vertical alignment using appropriate tools
pcs.measurementTask: Hold a plumb bob or long spirit level on the wall face over its full height and enter the largest deviation from plumb in mm (deviation; the guide sets no fixed target).
observables: Checks line, level and alignment with masons line, tube level and try square
Wall alignment over up to 3 m is within 5 mm
Internal squareness of the L corner is within 4 mm, and within 5 mm on the other side
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), pages 21 and 74

tolerance.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 74: Plumb to overall height ±5mm

nos.title: Carry out IPS / Tremix flooring works

elements.title: Carry out preparatory work prior to IPS / Tremix flooring
Check for line, level and alignment
Check the materials used for IPS / Tremix flooring in case of manual mixing
Check the materials used for IPS/Tremix flooring in case of machine mixing
Carry out IPS Flooring work
Carry out Tremix / VDF Flooring work

pcs.text: inspect the work area prior to concreting, ensure levelling in case of any undulations observed on the surface prior to concreting
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or concreting starts over undulations, wrong slope or honeycombs without inspection.
Meets standard: inspects the area, levels the undulations and deals with honeycombs before concreting.
Exceeds in places: checks levels across the area with tube level and straight edge and notes what was corrected.
Excellent: thorough pre-pour inspection; explains how base defects show up as cracks or uneven thickness.
observables: Inspects the base for undulations, slope and honeycombs before concreting
Levels high and low spots before the pour
Reports defects it cannot correct
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: ensure surface is prepared appropriately and report any deviation in slope and alignment in PCC
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or pours on a dirty, smooth base, or says nothing about a wrongly sloped PCC.
Meets standard: cleans and roughens the base as required and reports slope or alignment deviations to the supervisor.
Exceeds in places: measures the deviation and states it clearly when reporting, and wets the base before the pour.
Excellent: base fully ready and every deviation reported with facts and a practical fix suggested.
observables: Cleans the area properly before concreting
Roughens the surface where required
Reports deviations in slope and alignment of the PCC to the supervisor
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: report any gaps in formwork to avoid leakage
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or concreting goes ahead with open gaps in the formwork.
Meets standard: checks the formwork for gaps and reports or seals them before concreting.
Exceeds in places: checks the full run, including corners and bottom edges, and rechecks during the pour.
Excellent: no slurry loss at all; explains how leaks cause honeycombs and weak edges.
observables: Inspects formwork joints and edges for gaps
Has the formwork sealed so slurry cannot leak
Reports gaps it cannot seal to the supervisor
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: report any misalignment in formwork/reinforcement and ensure proper cover for reinforcement is provided
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or misses misaligned formwork or bars lying without cover.
Meets standard: checks alignment and cover and reports any misalignment before concreting.
Exceeds in places: checks cover blocks at regular spacing and that bars stay in place during the pour.
Excellent: thorough checks with clear reports; explains how low cover leads to rusting and cracking.
observables: Checks formwork and reinforcement are in true alignment
Checks the cover to reinforcement from the reference line
Reports misalignment or missing cover blocks before the pour
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: mark reference level on the wall &transfer this marking to all floor locations using appropriates tools
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or reference marks are missing, wrong or inconsistent between walls.
Meets standard: marks the reference level on the wall and transfers it to all floor locations with a tube level.
Exceeds in places: joins the marks with a line around the room and cross-checks them before use.
Excellent: accurate, complete level marking done quickly; explains how it controls floor level and slope.
observables: Marks the reference level 300 mm above finished floor level on the walls
Transfers it to all corners and floor locations with a tube level
Marks are clear, permanent and consistent around the room
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: mark flooring thickness level and provide dummy level dots at specified intervals for ensuring required slope
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or no level dots, or dots at wrong levels so the thickness and slope vary.
Meets standard: marks the floor thickness and fixes level dots at the specified intervals to the required slope.
Exceeds in places: checks each dot against the reference line and keeps the intervals regular.
Excellent: accurate grid of dots giving even thickness and slope; explains how the dots guide the levelling.
observables: Measures down from the reference line to mark the finished floor level
Fixes level dots at the specified intervals across the floor
Sets the dots to give the required slope
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: check the grade of cement prior to use in case of manual mixing
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses cement without checking grade or date, or uses lumpy cement.
Meets standard: checks the grade, batch date and week of manufacture and the condition of the bags.
Exceeds in places: uses older sound stock first and keeps checked bags stacked off the floor.
Excellent: careful checks every time; explains how grade and age affect concrete strength.
observables: Reads the grade on the cement bag
Checks the batch date and week of manufacture
Rejects bags with lumps or damage
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: ensure fine aggregate is sieved as per grade requirement
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses unsieved, dirty or silty sand.
Meets standard: sieves the sand to the required grade and uses only clean sieved sand.
Exceeds in places: checks the sand for silt and keeps sieved sand covered and separate.
Excellent: correct sand every time; explains how grading and silt affect the floor.
observables: Sieves the sand to the required grade
Removes stones, clay lumps and rubbish
Uses only clean sieved sand in the mix
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: check that concrete is mixed in appropriate proportion
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or mixes by guess with no check on the proportion.
Meets standard: checks that the concrete is mixed to the specified M20 proportion by measured batching.
Exceeds in places: uses gauge boxes for each batch and mixes thoroughly before adding water.
Excellent: consistent, correct mixes; explains what M20 means and how proportion affects strength.
observables: Checks that the mix proportion is M20 as specified
Batches cement, sand and aggregate by measured volume
Mixes until the concrete is uniform in colour
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: visually assess the concrete mix for usability and workability
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or uses concrete that is streaky, segregated, too dry or too wet.
Meets standard: checks colour, mixing and workability and keeps the water cement ratio as required.
Exceeds in places: spots extra water or segregation quickly and stops the batch before it is placed.
Excellent: sound judgement of every batch; explains how extra water weakens the floor surface.
observables: Concrete is mixed properly and uniform in colour
Workability suits placing and compacting, without segregation
Water added keeps to the required water cement ratio
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: notify superiors for detrimental quality of concrete
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or places poor concrete without telling anyone.
Meets standard: stops and reports poor concrete quality to the supervisor promptly.
Exceeds in places: reports clearly with the batch, time and defect, and holds the batch aside.
Excellent: reliable escalation every time; explains the risk of using poor concrete.
observables: Recognises poor concrete, such as segregated, stale or too wet
Stops using it and informs the supervisor at once
States what is wrong with the batch
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: ensure specified concrete mix is used at allocated location
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or places concrete without checking it is the grade specified for that location.
Meets standard: ensures the specified concrete, such as M20, is placed only at its allocated location.
Exceeds in places: checks the batch record or delivery note against the drawing before each pour.
Excellent: no mix-ups at all; explains why different areas need different grades.
observables: Confirms the concrete grade, such as M20, for each location before placing
Matches each batch to its location on the drawing
Does not place leftover concrete of another grade
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: check that panels prepared are of specified size and type
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or panels are oversized or of the wrong type and not checked.
Meets standard: checks every panel's size and type against the specification, none over 3 m.
Exceeds in places: also measures the diagonals so panels are square, and corrects errors before concreting.
Excellent: all panels correct and square; explains why panel size limits shrinkage cracks.
observables: Measures the panel sizes against the drawing
Checks that no panel exceeds 3 m
Checks the divider strip type matches the specification
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 23

pcs.text: fix the glass, aluminum or brass strip in cement mortar with their tops at appropriate level and according to slope
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or strips are loose, crooked or set at wrong levels.
Meets standard: fixes the strips firmly in mortar with tops at the finished level and slope.
Exceeds in places: strips are straight and vertical, checked with line and level, with neat junctions.
Excellent: all strips true to line, level and slope first time; explains how they control the floor level.
observables: Fixes the glass, aluminium or brass strips as per the drawing in proper sequence
Beds the strips firmly in cement mortar
Sets the strip tops at the finished floor level and slope
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 24

pcs.text: ensure panels are made as per specified size
pcs.measurementTask: Measure the spacing between glass strips at both ends of each panel and enter the largest deviation from the drawing spacing in mm (deviation; the guide sets no fixed target).
observables: Sets out the panels from the drawing before fixing the strips
No panel exceeds 3 m
Panels are square and of equal size
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 24

tolerance.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 75: Spacing between the glass panel (3 meter) ±10mm

pcs.text: ensure concrete is poured in alternate panels/specified panels as per requirement
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or pours adjoining panels together against the specified sequence.
Meets standard: pours alternate or specified panels in sequence, placing from one end to the other.
Exceeds in places: protects the edges of cast panels when filling the rest and keeps each pour continuous.
Excellent: well-planned pour sequence; explains how alternate panels control shrinkage cracks.
observables: Pours alternate or specified panels as required
Places concrete from one end of the panel to the other
Fills the remaining panels after the first ones have hardened
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 24

pcs.text: remove excess cement slurry and any marks on the surface
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or excess slurry and marks are left on the surface.
Meets standard: removes excess slurry and marks from the surface with straight edge and trowel.
Exceeds in places: cleans the strip tops and edges too, without disturbing the concrete.
Excellent: clean, mark-free surface throughout; explains why slurry build-up dusts and cracks.
observables: Removes excess slurry with straight edge and trowel
Cleans slurry and marks off the strips and edges
Surface is left free of marks
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 24

pcs.text: level the concrete surface with a straight edge and to the required finish with a wooden float / trowel
pcs.measurementTask: Hold a straight edge on the finished floor in several directions and enter the largest gap under it in mm (deviation; the guide sets no fixed target).
observables: Levels the concrete with a straight edge resting on the strips
Finishes the surface with a wooden float or trowel
Edges and corners are truly straight
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), pages 24 and 75

tolerance.source: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 75: Surface evenness ±3mm

pcs.text: spread cement punning over the IPS concrete for smooth finish surface and allow it to soak into the concrete, as per requirement
anchors: Below standard: not attempted, or the punning is thick or patchy, or spread on hardened concrete.
Meets standard: spreads punning thinly on green concrete, lets it soak in and trowels it smooth.
Exceeds in places: times the trowelling so the surface is dense and uniform, without trowel marks.
Excellent: smooth, hard, even finish; explains why thick punning crazes and how timing matters.
observables: Spreads neat cement punning thinly over the green concrete
Lets it soak in, then finishes with a metal float or trowel
Surface is smooth and even, with no dusting or crazing
pcs.observablesSource: CSDCI Assessment Guide, Mason General (CON/Q0103 ver. 1.0), page 24

pcs.text: provide construction joints and expansion joints as per requirement
